verdicts.why: Names a place that is unsafe in plain words; a bad referent, not a loaded word.
A plain name for the bang of a gun; no attitude toward the sound.
Names a person's standing without saying whether it is good or bad; the judgement lives in the modifier (good report, ill report), not the word.
A neutral name for a school document; the evaluation is its content, not an attitude in the word.
A plain name for a written assignment; describes without judging.
The furniture sense names a dressing table and carries none of the moral charge of the character-trait sense.
Names an end point in plain words; no attitude toward what ends.
A technical unit of geological time; purely descriptive.
A technical measure of a repeating cycle; purely descriptive.
A division of a hockey game; purely descriptive.
Names getting back to a former financial state without approving or disparaging the recoverer.
A plain industrial term for reclaiming materials; no attitude.
Literally re-cover, as an upholsterer does; purely descriptive.
A small mouthful, named plainly; no judgement of the food or the eater.
A brief sample of an experience, good or bad (a taste of freedom, a taste of defeat); the word itself takes no side.
The sense faculty, named plainly; purely descriptive.
The act of sensing by the taste buds; purely descriptive.
A computer expansion board; a technical name with no attitude.
A material, named plainly; purely descriptive.
A calling card, named plainly; the ceremony in the sentences belongs to the adjective, not the noun.
A posted notice; purely descriptive.
A golf scorecard; purely descriptive.
A menu; purely descriptive.
A batting order; purely descriptive.
Names someone's reserve without the disapproval of aloofness or standoffishness; the coolness is the referent, not an attitude in the word.
